ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, points D and E are the trisection points of $BC$, and $\triangle ADE$ is an equilateral triangle. What is the measure of $\angle BAC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
Solution: Since $E$ is the trisecting point of $BC$, and $\triangle ADE$ is an equilateral triangle,\\
$\therefore BD=DE=EC=AD=AE$, $\angle ADE=\angle AED=60^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle B=\angle BAD=\angle C=\angle EAC=30^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle BAC=180^\circ-\angle B-\angle C=\boxed{120^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, B, D, E, C are on the same horizontal straight line, in the order B-D-E-C; point A is above, and is connected respectively to B, D, E, C, forming the external triangle ABC and the internal triangle ADE. Reasoning: The problem statement gives that D, E are the trisection points of BC, so BD = DE = EC. Also because △ADE is an equilateral triangle, AD = DE = AE, and ∠ADE = ∠AED = 60°. Therefore AD = BD, AE = EC. In △ABD, DB is the reverse extension line of DE at point D, so ∠BDA = 180° - ∠ADE = 120°. Also AD = BD, therefore the two base angles of △ABD are equal, ∠BAD = ∠ABD = (180° - 120°)/2 = 30°. Similarly, in △AEC, EC is the reverse extension line of ED at point E, so ∠AEC = 180° - ∠AED = 120°; also AE = EC, therefore ∠EAC = ∠ACE = (180° - 120°)/2 = 30°. Finally, ∠BAC = ∠BAD + ∠DAE + ∠EAC = 30° + 60° + 30° = 120°.
